meta.title: {name} — Engineering for a More Accessible World
meta.description: Mechanical engineer designing wheelchair adaptations, accessibility solutions and custom assistive devices for people with disabilities.

image.alt: Wheelchair-mounted tray with a custom joystick control and blue ball grip
image.caption: Custom flip-over joystick and flat-switch mount

specialisation.title: Mechanical design where the user comes first.
specialisation.lead: My work sits between mechanical engineering and rehabilitation — making devices that are strong, light and simple enough to use every day.

areas.title: Wheelchair adaptations
areas.body: Mounts, trays, positioning aids and frame modifications that fit the chair and the person in it.

areas.title: Assistive devices
areas.body: Custom mechanical tools for daily living, shaped around grip, reach and strength.

areas.title: Accessibility solutions
areas.body: Ramps, access aids and environmental fixes that remove barriers in the built world.

areas.title: User-centred design
areas.body: Co-design with users and therapists, from first interview to field-tested prototype.

featuredProjects.title: Featured projects
featuredProjects.lead: Case studies from my university internships — from problem definition through fabrication and testing.

process.title: From a real barrier to a working device.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: Understand the person, the task and the barrier.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Concepts, CAD, analysis and material selection.

steps.title: Validate
steps.body: Test with users and iterate until it works.

contactBand.title: Looking for a mechanical engineer in assistive technology?
contactBand.body: I'd be glad to talk about roles, projects or collaborations.
